decision.retrieved_from: Nebraska Advance Sheets PDF via CourtListener cluster 10813510; the citation chart was re-extracted with per-word coordinates so the two table columns line up correctly
decision.ai_tool_found: asserted by appellee to be generative AI; appellant's counsel denied AI use and blamed a cracked laptop screen and filing the wrong draft. The court held its analysis was the same either way.
decision.table_note: Records below reproduce the court's own chart, 321 Neb. at 47–49, which lists each citation in the appellant's brief and the result of the court's review.

offending.as_cited: Kennedy v. Kennedy, 27 Neb. App. 510, 934 N.W.2d 57 (2019)
offending.quoted_text: In Kennedy v. Kennedy, 27 Neb. App. 510, 934 N.W.2d 57 (2019), the court reversed a parenting time order because it lacked specific findings explaining why the reduced parenting time was in the child's best interest.
offending.filing: Brief for appellant at 13 (and four further places)
offending.court_quote: “Kennedy v. Kennedy” is the name of a real case decided by the Nebraska Court of Appeals in an unpublished memorandum opinion filed in 2019, which does not correspond to the citation given. Furthermore, the unpublished memorandum opinion does not stand for the proposition advanced by Jason. … Further, Jason's brief includes a block quotation from “Kennedy v. Kennedy” that does not exist in the unpublished memorandum opinion; nor does it appear to exist anywhere in Nebraska case law. Chart: “Fictitious case using real case name from unpublished memorandum opinion • Cited and quoted five times throughout brief • Quotes and holding do not exist in the real unpublished memorandum opinion or other Nebraska case law”
offending.what_actually_exists: Kennedy v. Kennedy, No. A-18-824, 2019 WL 2754981 (Neb. App. July 2, 2019), an unpublished memorandum opinion that does not discuss parenting time and does not mention any need for specific findings; it does not appear at 27 Neb. App. 510 or 934 N.W.2d 57.

offending.as_cited: State on behalf of Maddox S. v. Matthew E., 23 Neb. App. 500, 874 N.W.2d 211 (2016)
offending.cited_case_name: State on behalf of Maddox S. v. Matthew E.
offending.court_quote: Chart: “State on behalf of Maddox S. v. Matthew E., 23 Neb. App. 500, 874 N.W.2d 211 (2016) — • Incorrect citation • Does not support cited proposition • Fictitious quotations”
offending.what_actually_exists: The court found the citation incorrect, the case not to support the proposition cited, and the quotations fictitious.

offending.quoted_text: Parenting arrangements should ensure frequent, continuing, and meaningful contact with both parents as is in the child's best interests.
offending.court_quote: For example, Jason's brief purports to quote Neb. Rev. Stat. § 43-2923(1) (Reissue 2016) as stating, “‘Parenting arrangements should ensure frequent, continuing, and meaningful contact with both parents as is in the child's best interests.’” However, § 43-2923 actually states in part, “The best interest of the child require: (1) A parenting arrangement … .” Chart: “Real statute • Fictitious quotations and misleading application throughout brief”
offending.what_actually_exists: § 43-2923 is a real statute whose text begins “The best interests of the child require: (1) A parenting arrangement …”; the quoted sentence does not appear in it.

offending.quoted_text: A party is entitled to be informed of the issues raised, and cannot be expected to defend against a theory not disclosed in the pleadings.
offending.court_quote: Simons v. Simons does not support this proposition or address the denial of attorney fees. The only mention of attorney fees in Simons is in the standard of review in a section discussing alimony. Further, Jason's brief provides, “‘A party is entitled to be informed of the issues raised, and cannot be expected to defend against a theory not disclosed in the pleadings.’ Simons v. Simons, 312 Neb. 136, 147, 978 N.W.2d 121, 131 (2022).” This quote attributed to Simons does not exist within the case, nor does it appear to exist in Nebraska case law. Simons is misstated and misquoted several more times throughout the brief.
offending.what_actually_exists: Simons v. Simons, 312 Neb. 136, 978 N.W.2d 121 (2022) is a real Nebraska Supreme Court decision; it does not address denial of attorney fees except in the standard of review of an alimony section, and it contains no such quotation.
